About Event

Your agent works. Then the process crashes, a tool times out, or a human approval takes longer than expected.
Can it pick up where it left off?
Join HackerSquad and Diamond Sponsor Diagrid at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco on December 11 for a full-day hackathon focused on building agents that recover from interruptions and finish what they started.
The challenge: build an agent or workflow, make it durable with Diagrid, then interrupt it mid-run and show us what happens next.
Durable execution lets an application preserve progress and resume after an interruption. You’ll put that idea to work—and put your project to the test.
What you can build
Bring your own use case. Build something practical, experimental, or just fun:
An agent that survives a crash: Interrupt a research assistant or multi-step automation and demonstrate how it resumes.

A workflow that waits for a human: Pause for a review or approval, then continue when the decision arrives.

A team of agents that finishes the job: Coordinate handoffs and show what happens when one part gets interrupted.

A game that remembers: Build a durable dungeon master or another interactive experience that keeps its progress through a restart.

These are starting points. The common thread is using Diagrid for durable execution and demonstrating recovery in your project.
The live recovery demo
Your final demo should tell a clear story:
What did you build? Show the task your agent or workflow is trying to complete.

What went wrong? Kill the process or introduce an interruption.

What happened next? Restart it and show how it recovers, what progress it preserves, and whether any work gets repeated.

Start with a simple kill-and-restart test, or go further with timeouts, rate limits, interrupted handoffs, and chaos testing.
Getting started
Diagrid will provide starter examples and technical mentorship to help you build. We’ll share the recommended setup, supported technology options, and any account requirements before the event.
Explore the Diagrid AI docs and quickstart examples for an early look.
Prize categories and judging details will be announced.
Who should join
AI engineers, backend and platform developers, technical founders, and builders curious about making agents more reliable. You don’t need prior experience with durable execution, but come ready to write code and test your assumptions.
Bring your laptop, an idea, and a willingness to kill what you just built.

About Event

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.

If you're excited about the future of AI, agents and scientific discovery, we'll see you there...

People who build for a living: ML engineers, software developers, and agent builders who can take a half-formed scientific problem and ship something that runs by Sunday.

Tracks
Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.
Track B: Build a Dataset or Meta-Analysis

What have you always wanted the literature to tell you, but could never read fast enough to find out? Draft the queries, run them across thousands of papers, sharpen and re-run until the results hold the specific pieces you care about. Then the real work: find the pattern in what you assembled that no single paper could show you, and demo that.

Assemble a pipeline that designs biology to a spec you choose, from a single protein up to a multi-gene system. You set the constraints; the models generate candidates and evolve them toward something that could hold up in a real cell. Could the literature reveal the most promising design space for a generative model to explore? Free Paperclip API access, access to Proto , Claude API credits, and compute and credits from our sponsors.

What happens to what I build afterward?

You keep it. Teams are free to open-source, continue building, or spin their project into something bigger.

Check out visual of our AI Multiplayer Hackathon where AI agents make films, play games with you and interview you, plus try each sponsor's tool live to make it easy to understand at  https://crewbasecollective.com/aim-hack-visual
AI has learned to talk. Now it is learning to act: to make its own decisions, collaborate with other agents, and share spaces with humans.
Multiplayer AI is a hackathon for building AI agents that behave like living characters. They move, interact, compete, cooperate, decide outcomes, and even teach humans. There is no single chatbot and no fixed script, only agents with their own goals, personalities and minds, in worlds you create.
Whether you are a developer, designer, game builder, ML engineer, product manager or storyteller, this is your chance to build what comes after chat: AI that plays, performs and teaches.
The Challenge
Most AI today is one human talking to one assistant. The next step is multiplayer: many agents interacting with each other and with humans, where the outcome is not scripted but emerges from what the agents decide.
Your challenge is to build an experience where multiple AI agents come alive as visible characters that think, act, move and make decisions, shaping a film, a game, or a real person's growth.
What to Build
Choose one of the three tracks and build a working, visual, multi-agent experience.
Every project must include:
Characters: each agent has a visual identity, such as an avatar, sprite, or 2D or 3D model
Visual output: an animated video, a running simulation, or a playable game
Movement and action: characters move, react and act on screen, not just output text
At least three agents with their own goals, roles or personalities
Visible decisions: a log or ledger showing what the agents decided and why
Projects score higher with:
3D: 2D projects are welcome, but 3D is encouraged and scores higher
ML and trained agents: agents that learn, adapt or are trained, through reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, learned behaviour, or memory that changes their decisions over time
Voice: agents that speak with their own voices
Tracks
Track 1: Agent Animated Film
Create a short animated film where the plot is written by agents, not by you. You set up the world, the characters and the opening event. From there the agents interact, make choices, and decide how the story ends.
What this track involves:
You set the world, the characters and the opening event
Agents interact and decide every plot beat, including the ending
Characters are animated, moving and reacting on screen
The same setup produces different endings across runs
The output is a 1–3 minute animated short
Examples: A heist crew with a hidden traitor, where the agents decide whether the heist succeeds. Survivors on a sinking spaceship fighting over a single escape pod. A courtroom where lawyer, witness and jury agents reach their own verdict.
Track 2: Co-op Multiplayer Game
Build a multiplayer game where humans and AI agents share the same world as equal players. The agents are not NPCs waiting for instructions. They have their own goals, memories and plans, and they act whether or not a human is involved.
What this track involves:
At least 2 human players and 3 agent players in one visual game world
Agents act independently with their own goals and memory
Agents can ally with players, trade with them, compete or betray them
At least one major world event is caused by agents alone
Examples: A survival island where agent tribes choose to welcome or betray human players. A trading town where agent merchants strike deals and hold grudges. A social deduction game where the impostor could be a human or an agent.
Track 3: Grow with Agents
The roles are reversed. Usually humans train AI; here, agents train humans. Agents step into expert roles such as interviewer, examiner, professor, coach, boss or client, and the human learns, practises, gets tested and improves through a visual, interactive simulation.
What this track involves:
Agents play expert roles such as interviewer, examiner, coach or boss, as visible characters
At least 2–3 agents coordinate about the human
Agents adapt to how the human is performing
The session ends with a clear result and evidence-based feedback
Examples: A 3D interview panel that questions you, deliberates and gives a verdict. An office simulator with an agent boss, teammates and a difficult client. A driving test with an agent examiner in a simulated city. A sales call where you pitch to a buying committee that pushes back on every claim.
Who Should Join
Developers, game builders, ML engineers, 3D artists, designers, product managers and storytellers. Join solo or in a team of up to four.
Build agents that do not just talk. Build agents that play, perform and teach.
Sponsors
Bruin (Main Sponsor)
Bruin is an all-in-one data and AI platform that eliminates fragmented data tools by bringing everything into one unified workspace. It transforms raw data into actionable AI-powered insights in seconds, directly within Slack, Microsoft Teams, and your browser. Check out https://getbruin.com
AdaL
AdaL is an automation-first agent harness designed to get more done with less of your time. She combines personality, skills, and memory to become a personalized agent that can work alongside you. Check out https://adalagent.ai
BAND
BAND helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done. Check out https://www.band.ai
Finch
Finch provides agent skills that give AI agents reusable capabilities for performing specific tasks. Skills can help make agents more useful, structured, and consistent. Check out https://www.finchtech.ai
Casuro
Casuro.ai is an AI-powered recruitment platform that helps companies streamline hiring through intelligent assessments, voice AI interviews, and real-world case study challenges. It evaluates candidates based on their skills, problem-solving abilities, and how effectively they work with AI, enabling teams to make faster, fairer, and more informed hiring decisions. Check out casuro.ai

About Event

Round two of the SF × MIT hack days, this time on peptides. Sundai Club builds at MIT, we build at AGI House SF.
Peptides are short chains of amino acids. GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide are peptides, and they've become some of the best-selling medicines in the world. A model can propose thousands of candidate sequences in an afternoon. The hard part is knowing which ones will bind their target, hold up in the body and stay safe, and that checking is the job we want agents doing: run the simulation, grade the result, get better each run.
Tracks:
Peptide design: agents that propose sequences against a target and score them with structure prediction and docking before anything gets synthesized.

Evidence engine: search and grade the published human data on peptides, from trials to adverse event reports, so every claim comes with its sources.

Evals for science: graders that tell you whether a predicted binder or stability score holds up, so the loop can improve without a human checking every step.

RSIhouse.ai - a weekly open neutral space for hacks and dinners exclusively for recursive self improvement. We touch on topics of post-training, evals, harness engineering, self-play and swarm intelligence. Every week we explore the limits of RSI.
Autolab.ai is building infrastructure for the RSI. Starting with the evals, Autolab enables fully autonomous continual learning and ownership of your own enterprise AI models that get better with every API call you make.
Superradiant is a research lab building self-improving agents who are bringing the rapid advances in mathematics to the sciences. Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is one of the most celebrated festivals in India. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. During Diwali, people decorate their homes with colorful lights, candles, and beautiful rangoli designs. Families celebrate by sharing sweets, exchanging gifts, wearing new clothes, and enjoying fireworks. It is a time of happiness, love, hope, and togetherness.

Tracks
🛡️ Security — Attack & Defend
Build AI agents that simulate cyberattacks and defend systems against potential threats in a controlled environment.
Red Agent identifies vulnerabilities, tests system defenses, and exposes security weaknesses. Blue Agent detects threats, analyzes vulnerabilities, and strengthens system security. The Red Agent shares its findings with the Blue Agent, which uses them to detect threats and improve system defenses.
Example: One agent attempts to breach a test application while the other detects the attack and recommends security fixes.
💹 Finance — Analyze & Trade
Build AI agents that research financial markets, identify investment opportunities, and make data-driven trading decisions. Analyst Agent gathers market data, tracks trends, and identifies potential investment opportunities. Trader Agent uses market insights to make decisions and execute simulated trades. The Analyst Agent shares market insights with the Trader Agent, which uses them to make informed trading decisions.
Example: One agent tracks stock trends and identifies opportunities while another executes simulated trades based on its analysis.

Visual Agent generates campaign images, promotional creatives, and marketing videos. Copy Agent creates matching headlines, captions, ad copy, and social media content. Most agents today can talk. Fewer can produce real output, operate real software, and carry context from one session to the next. This hackathon is about building agents that do all three.

About Event

Building long-running agents? Want to talk with people in the same boat? Want to get a brief workout in the Marina?
Come for a run on Wednesday November 18th with the MIT & Harvard engineers from Subconscious.dev and friends from RSIHouse & Sundai.
We'll run a casual 4 miles at a talkative pace, and leave plenty of time to chat afterwards at Equator Coffees by Fort Mason.
This is an open invite, honeypots welcome . See you there!
🏃‍♀️ 🏃⌛️ ☀️
Subconscious.dev is an inference provider designed for long-running agents. We've made a series of proprietary enhancements in our inference infrastructure to serve open weight models faster, cheaper, and more accurately on tasks requiring more than 200k tokens. You can learn more at https://subconscious.dev
🥇
With support from:
Sundai.club is the largest AI hacker community born out of Harvard & MIT that shipped more than 130+ hackathons back-to-back in the last 2.5 years - one for every sunday without stopping. 1000+ projects, with many funded by VCs, YC, etc.
RSIhouse.ai - a weekly open neutral space for hacks and dinners exclusively for recursive self improvement. We touch on topics of post-training, evals, harness engineering, self-play and swarm intelligence. Every week we explore the limits of RSI.
Autolab.ai is building infrastructure for the RSI. Starting with the evals, Autolab enables fully autonomous continual learning and ownership of your own enterprise AI models that get better with every API call you make.
